title: An improved compact formulation for the assortment optimization problem with small consideration sets
contribution: An improved compact MILP for assortment optimization under the k-product non-parametric ranking-based choice model, with a very tight continuous relaxation, that a general-purpose solver solves to provable optimality for up to 200 products, 100,000 customer classes and k = 5 in a few minutes (abstract).
problem_entry: Assortment optimization with small consideration sets is NP-hard already for k = 2, and the best approximation method stays 0.3-0.5% from optimal at k = 4, 100 products and 10,000 classes (abstract).
key_idea: Improve the literature's compact MILP for the full non-parametric ranking-based model into a compact model for small consideration sets with a very tight continuous relaxation, solved by a general-purpose solver (abstract).
assumptions: Customer classes with preference lists of at most k products; each customer buys the most preferred product offered (abstract).
experiments: An extensive set of experiments: provable optima for up to 200 products, 100,000 customer classes and k = 5 in a few minutes; no solver, hardware or baseline run named in the abstract (abstract).
positioning: Builds on a compact MILP from the literature for the full ranking-based model and measures itself against the best approximation method (its guarantee and its empirical 0.3-0.5% gaps) (abstract).
writing: Problem, hardness, the best prior method's guarantee and empirical gap, the formulation, then the size reached and the runtime (abstract).
limits_future: No limitation or future direction stated in the abstract (abstract).

method_links.note: Step 1 (joint, 2025): the answer is a tightened compact model handed to a general-purpose solver, not a dedicated algorithm.
Step 2 (joint): the model is fitted to the problem class at hand (small consideration sets rather than the full ranking model), but by tightening the continuous relaxation, not by removing variables.

transferable: Before building an approximation scheme for a choice-model assortment problem, tighten the compact MILP of the general model to the restricted preference structure and measure whether a stock solver proves optimality at the instance sizes the approximation papers report, and beyond (abstract).

quotes.text: we propose an improved compact model that features a very tight continuous relaxation and can be easily solved with a general-purpose solver
This problem is known to be NP-hard even when k is equal to 2.

title: Solving Congested Facility Location by Branch-and-Cut
contribution: A ROADEF 2016 abstract that solves congested facility location by a perspective reformulation of the MINLP followed by generalized Benders cuts that project the allocation variables out, in a branch-and-cut framework with a simplified implementation (abstract).
problem_entry: Congested facility location extends the capacitated (or p-median) problem: higher load means longer waiting times, so the diseconomies of scale are convex cost functions of the facility load (abstract).
key_idea: Perspective reformulation first (much better continuous lower bounds), then generalized Benders cuts obtained by projecting the allocation variables out of it, inside branch-and-cut (abstract).
assumptions: Capacitated or p-median location with convex, load-dependent congestion costs; the standard model is an MINLP (abstract).
proof_devices: perspective reformulation of the standard MINLP (abstract)
generalized Benders cuts by projecting out the allocation variables (abstract)
experiments: none in the abstract; results were to be presented at the conference (abstract).
positioning: An extension of capacitated / p-median facility location (abstract); the conference counterpart of the congested case of S023 (inferred).
writing: A talk abstract that announces the implementation details and the results for the talk itself (abstract).

method_links.note: Steps 3-4 (joint): the allocation variables are projected out (Benders) and the master is solved by branch-and-cut, but only after the model has been strengthened by a perspective reformulation, the reverse of the order in the method's one-line rule.

transferable: When a location model carries convex load-dependent costs, take the perspective reformulation first and derive the generalized Benders cuts from it rather than from the standard MINLP (abstract).

quotes.text: We finally derive generalized Benders cuts by projecting out allocation variables from the perspective reformulation.
This reformulation greatly improves the quality of lower bounds of the underlying continuous relaxation.
